beats.lead: A strawberry has hundreds of seeds on the outside.
beats.text: None of them are actually seeds, and the fruit isn't a berry.
beats.note: Botanically, a strawberry fails the definition of a berry on every count that matters.

beats.lead: A true berry has to grow from a single ovary.
beats.text: A strawberry's flower has dozens of separate ones.
beats.note: That single-ovary rule is why bananas, grapes, tomatoes and even cucumbers count as true berries, while strawberries, raspberries and blackberries don't.

beats.lead: The red part you eat isn't fruit tissue at all.
beats.text: It's the swollen base of the flower.
beats.note: What botanists call the receptacle grows large and fleshy around the true fruits, rather than the flesh coming from any ovary wall, which is how a true berry is built.

beats.lead: Those yellow dots on the surface
beats.text: are the actual fruits, not seeds.
beats.note: Each dot is a separate dry fruit called an achene, and each one holds a single true seed sealed inside it.

beats.text: The avocado, with its single huge seed, meets the botanical definition of a berry. The strawberry, with hundreds of visible seeds, doesn't.

beats.line: Every strawberry is a lie told by hundreds of tiny fruits at once.
